subject: We analyzed 10,000 users and found something shocking
preview_text: 92% of couples skip this one feature—and it's costing them the spark. See what we discovered.
body_paragraphs: Here's the thing about planning dates: most couples think they're good at it. But after looking at data from 10,000 SoulPlan users, we found a pattern that honestly scared us. The couples who keep the spark alive? They're not just randomly picking ideas. They're using one specific tool that 92% of users ignore. And those who ignore it? Their date frequency drops by 40% within two months.

We expected to see the usual stuff—budget constraints, time issues, lack of inspiration. Instead, the biggest predictor of a dying spark was simple: not tracking what you've already done. Without a history, couples accidentally repeat the same tired dinner-and-a-movie routine until it feels like a chore. The data doesn't lie: variety is the secret sauce, and most people are cooking with just salt.

That's why we built the date history tracker. It's not just a log—it's your relationship's memory bank. Every time you tap 'Add to History' after a date, you're telling the app what worked (and what bombed). Then our AI uses that to serve up fresh ideas you'll actually love. One couple told us it saved them from their 15th Italian restaurant in a row. No judgment, but you deserve better.

Open SoulPlan right now and go to your date history. Check if you've logged your last three dates. If you haven't, start today—it takes 10 seconds. And here's the kicker: couples who log at least 5 dates see a 70% boost in feeling 'excited' about their next plan. Don't be the 92%. Be the exception.
